sections.h2: What sets Thomas County apart in southwest Georgia?
sections.html:
Thomas County sits on the Florida line and is built around Thomasville, the county seat and its largest city. The General Assembly created it on December 23, 1825, from parts of Decatur and Irwin counties, and Colquitt, Brooks and Grady were later carved partly out of its original land, per Wikipedia.

The county covers 552 square miles, almost all of it land. Water drains three ways: the northwest half feeds the Ochlockonee River basin, the northeastern edge feeds the Suwannee basin, and the southeast drains toward the Aucilla River, which rises inside the county. The Red Hills region is centered here. Neighbors are Colquitt, Brooks, Grady and Mitchell counties in Georgia, plus Jefferson and Leon counties across the state line in Florida.

Besides Thomasville, the county holds the cities of Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs and Pavo, and the town of Ochlocknee. Barwick and Pavo reach into Brooks County, and Meigs reaches into Mitchell. Two public school systems serve the area: Thomasville City Schools inside the city, and Thomas County Schools everywhere else. A seller whose house falls on one side of that line is selling to a different set of school-minded buyers than a neighbor a few blocks away.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Thomas County housing?
sections.html:
Owners hold a clear majority of Thomas County homes, and values sit well above the other three counties in this group. QuickFacts lists 63.8% of housing units as owner-occupied for 2020-2024.

The Census Bureau counted 45,798 residents in 2020 and estimates 46,368 in mid-2025, a 1.3% gain on the 2020 base. There are 18,684 households, and 21.0% of residents are 65 or older. With 203 building permits in 2025, new construction competes lightly with resale homes, so an older house on a Thomasville street is not up against a flood of new listings.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Thomas County?
sections.html:
Two separate offices split the work. The tax commissioner bills and collects, and the board of tax assessors sets values and takes exemption applications.

The Thomas County tax commissioner works from 225 N. Broad Street in Thomasville, 31792, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 2175, Thomasville, GA 31799. The phone is (229) 225-4136, and the office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with a posted holiday closing schedule.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, delinquent balances, tax sale payoff amounts
  • Tax assessor: values, returns, homestead applications, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and tax liens
  • City tax departments: Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville each collect their own city tax

The county site explains that county commissioners set the county rate and the county school board sets the school rate. The state sets its own small levy by law. A Thomasville address can therefore carry a city bill in addition to the county bill, so ask each office what you owe before a closing.

sections.h2: When is Thomas County property tax due?
sections.html:
Property taxes are due every November 15, and the county honors mail postmarked by that date. A missing bill does not excuse the debt, according to the county's own information page.

Delinquent balances change on the 16th of each month, so a payoff quote is only good for the month it is given. Mobile home penalties are added each April 2. If a return is required and not filed, the county page lists a 10% penalty on the value that was not returned, plus interest.

  • Regular property tax: due November 15
  • Mobile homes: penalties added April 2
  • Delinquent amounts: recalculated on the 16th
  • Late return: 10% on the unreported value plus interest

The tax commissioner decides when tax sales happen, once or twice a year, and asks owners to call for the exact amount due before the sale date. Treat any dollar figure from an old bill as out of date.

sections.h2: What happens to Thomas County tax when you sell a house?
sections.html:
The seller owes the tax for the year if they owned the home on January 1. The state revenue department says Georgia has no partial-year refund, so a sale on January 2 still leaves the full year with the person who held title on January 1.

In practice the closing attorney asks the tax commissioner for the amount due on the parcel and pays it from the seller's proceeds, or the contract divides the year between buyer and seller. Ask the commissioner's office for the current figure in writing and ask whether any city tax applies. Unpaid tax can be turned into a lien recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and that lien has to be cleared before a buyer's title company will close.

If a house is behind on tax and also needs work, a buyer who purchases as-is can take over the paperwork and settle the balance at the table. That route skips listing prep, but it does not erase the debt. The tax is paid either way.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Thomas County value?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Thomas County Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. The 45-day rule comes from the Georgia Department of Revenue, and the Thomas County page cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 for the appeal itself.

The state allows a challenge on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption. The appeal form must name one of three paths: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. The county page says that if the assessors and owner cannot agree, the appeal is forwarded to the Board of Equalization automatically. Complaints about the tax rate itself are outside an assessment appeal.

  • Deadline: 45 days from the notice mailing date
  • Where to file: the Board of Tax Assessors
  • Next step if unresolved: Board of Equalization, then Superior Court

Assessments rest on 40% of fair market value as of January 1, and the county's page defines market value to include distress sales, short sales, bank sales and auction sales. That matters if your house sold under pressure, since such a sale can serve as evidence of value.

sections.h2: Which Thomas County exemptions matter before you sell?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one, and the application goes to the tax assessor's office. The county deadline is April 1, and an application received after that date starts with the following year.

You can file any time during the year, but the date that counts for the current bill is April 1. Thomas County says it offers local homestead exemptions that are more favorable than the state's version, and the assessor can tell you the current amounts. Ask for them rather than assuming a number.

For a seller, the practical point is to confirm the exemption is on the parcel before you list. A buyer's lender and the closing attorney will both look at the tax bill, and a missing exemption raises the figure they see. A new owner has to apply on their own, and a sale in the middle of the year does not carry the seller's filing forward.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Thomas County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Thomas County tax commissioner at (229) 225-4136 on weekdays between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. The office is at 225 N. Broad Street in Thomasville. For questions about value or an exemption, ask for the tax assessor's office instead.

faqs.q: What date is Thomas County property tax due?
faqs.a: November 15 each year, and mail postmarked by that date is honored. Delinquent amounts change on the 16th of each month, and mobile home penalties are added on April 2.

faqs.q: Does a sale cancel the year's tax in Thomas County?
faqs.a: No. Georgia does not refund tax for part of a year, and the person who owned the home on January 1 is responsible for that year's bill. The closing attorney normally pays the balance from the seller's proceeds, or the contract splits it.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal a Thomas County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors, and choose the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator on the appeal form.

faqs.q: Do Thomasville and the smaller cities bill their own tax?
faqs.a: Yes. According to the county tax commissioner's page, Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville each collect their own city taxes. Contact the city's tax department for that bill, in addition to the county tax commissioner.
